title: Behavior of the transfer machine
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a finite input word over an alphabet of symbols, and let $w$ be another finite word over that alphabet. Choose distinct indices $\mathrm{src},\mathrm{dst}\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ and a configuration $d$ on input $x$ whose state is the sweep phase. Suppose that, for every integer offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, the source tape of $d$ at the cell $p$ steps from its initial head position agrees with the buffer storing $w$ at offset $p$. After $2|w|+2$ steps, the transfer machine is in the done phase; it has erased the source tape and written the buffered word on the destination tape at offsets $0,\ldots,|w|-1$, leaving every other tape cell unchanged. It does not enter the done phase at any earlier step. At every step up to and including step $2|w|+2$, the source and destination heads lie between one cell to the left of their respective initial positions and $|w|$ cells to their right, inclusive, while every other work-tape head remains at its initial position.
